verification.notes: Both Archive.org originals matched the item metadata checksums and are byte-identical. The exact embedded bundle identity was checked before recording this source.

availability.notes: The maintainer designated this build unavailable with no currently marketed App Store alternative. Apple's US lookup for the exact com.nabilchatbi.Ricky bundle identifier returned zero results on 2026-07-17. This records project test scope, not a legal conclusion.

reports.summary: Launches on Windows and renders a stable main menu without reproducing the two startup red-black-tree crashes.
milestones: Rendered the Ricky main menu with Story Mode, Custom Levels, and Setting options.
Remained alive at the menu for a controlled 30-second observation.
reports.blocker: Gameplay, touch input, audio, saving, and network behavior have not yet been validated.
reports.notes: Tested from a clean committed tree using bundled default options only. The window was captured for visual verification and the tester then stopped the process. Automated Windows message injection did not produce an SDL touch event and is not treated as evidence that input is broken.

reports.summary: Reaches the first playable Story level on Windows through controlled process-scoped foreground input and primes Ricky's packetized MP3 AudioQueue without the prior format error or output-pointer panic.
milestones: Navigated Story Mode, New Game, PLAY, and both story advances using process-scoped foreground input.

Entered the first playable Story level, was sent a two-second hold on the on-screen right movement control through the verified tapHLE window, and remained alive for approximately 18 seconds after level entry.

Completed the previously failing AudioQueuePrime path after Ricky enqueued its three directly described MP3 buffers; error -66681, MP3 decode warnings, and the non-null output-pointer panic did not recur.
reports.blocker: Audible audio output and continuity, action buttons, level completion, hazards/death/restart, saving, and long-session behavior of the 0x40-byte allocation quarantine have not been validated.
reports.notes: Tested from a clean exact-commit release build after a full Archive.org verification of the IPA immediately before the run, using bundled default options and a 480x320 client. Every input event revalidated that the foreground window belonged to the spawned tapHLE process. A System.Drawing Graphics.CopyFromScreen capture of the OpenGL window returned a black bitmap and was excluded from evidence; it is not evidence of a rendering regression. Audio remains partial because this automated run proved queue decode/prime progress and process survival, not audible output.

reports.summary: Reproduces the first playable Story level and movement-input milestone on Windows, then closes naturally through Ricky's secondary Mono pthread exit path.
milestones: Navigated Story Mode, New Game, PLAY, and both story advances with process-scoped foreground input in a fresh sandbox.
Reached the first playable Story level, sent a two-second hold to the established on-screen right movement control, and remained alive for a further ten-second observation.

Processed applicationDidResignActive and applicationWillTerminate after a PID-verified WM_CLOSE, then exited with code 0 inside five seconds without forced termination, panic output, or a new Windows Application Error event.
reports.blocker: Default Windows-device audibility, action buttons, level completion, hazards/death/restart, saving, network behavior, and long-session behavior of the 0x40-byte allocation quarantine have not been validated.
reports.notes: The full Archive.org content-hash, embedded identity, and tapHLE --info verification was repeated immediately before recording this report. The exact release binary identified itself as e2d51c6c. Every input reacquired and verified the spawned process's 480x320 foreground window. A separate failed-focus attempt was discarded before its first tap. The successful Wave File Writer output was a valid 39.46-second 44.1 kHz stereo signed 16-bit PCM capture containing non-silent signal, but audio remains partial because the default device was not heard and the multi-context wave-backend attribution caveat still applies.
